page: Microsoft Azure DC48as_cc_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCACCV5 family, powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and single-core CPU capabilities. The instance scores in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as the Passmark CPU score. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, with the Passmark CPU encryption test placing in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top 10%, although raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall within the middle 50%.

Multi-threaded decompression and image processing benchmarks also rank in the top 25%. However, text processing, database operations, and static web serving throughput remain in the middle 50%. For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing and text generation speeds for small 135M parameter models, but performance drops to average for 7B models and is poor for large 70B parameter text generation. This profile makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded computational tasks, software compilation, and moderate database workloads, while large-scale language model inference represents a clear performance tradeoff.
